title: Akira
lede: Katsuhiro Otomo’s 1988 animated film of his manga, set in a Neo-Tokyo of densely drawn night towers, through which motorcycles leave trails of colored light.
summary: The founding work of Japanese cyberpunk: a detailed night Neo-Tokyo and light trails from speeding bikes. Katsuhiro Otomo, Tokyo Movie Shinsha, 1988.

creator.name: Katsuhiro Otomo (director); Tokyo Movie Shinsha (animation studio)

evidence.note: Based on the Wikipedia articles on the film and on cyberpunk, read as wikitext on 2026-10-02. No image of the film was inspected for this record.

styles.note: The style record names Akira as one of the two works that set the look of cyberpunk. The British Film Institute calls it a vital cornerstone of the genre.

context: Wikipedia: “The Japanese cyberpunk subgenre began in 1982 with the debut of Katsuhiro Otomo’s manga series Akira, with its 1988 anime film adaptation (also directed by Otomo) popularizing the subgenre.” [Cyberpunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk).

The film was animated by Tokyo Movie Shinsha and distributed by Toho. Wikipedia: “The British Film Institute describes Akira as a vital cornerstone of the cyberpunk genre, along with Blade Runner and Neuromancer.” [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akira_(1988_film)).

Dave Kehr of the *Chicago Tribune* praised its “animation-specific ideas: Vehicles leave little color trails as they roar through the night”. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akira_(1988_film)).
interpretation: Akira adds speed and violence to the night city of [Blade Runner](ref:blade-runner-1982). Its light trails are an early form of the style’s motion: light that smears as it moves.
It ties the style to Japan and to animation, which later games and anime continued.
borrow: Show motion as a trail of colored light behind a moving element, not as a blur of the whole scene.
Draw a city as a mass of many small lit windows to suggest scale and density.
